chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamdani (mercy of God be upon him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhar, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them all)

He said: A man stood before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and asked, 'O Commander of the Faithful! With what did you recognize your Lord?' He replied, 'Through the abolishment of resolve and the invalidation of ambition. When I had an ambition, something obstructed it between me and it. And when I made a decision, the Divine Decree opposed my resolve. I knew that the Planner was other than me.' The man asked, 'Then with what did you thank His blessings?' He answered, 'I looked at a tribulation which He diverted from me and afflicted someone else with it. I learned that He had bestowed favor upon me, so I thanked Him.' The man asked, 'Why do you desire to meet Him?' He replied, 'Because I saw that He chose for me the religion of His angels, Messengers, and Prophets. I knew that He who honored me with this would not forget me, so I desired to meet Him.'
ai.seo_question: How does one recognize God and express gratitude according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the epistemological foundation of *ma'rifah* (gnosis), asserting that true recognition of God arises from experiencing the transition from human volition to divine decree (*fals al-arad*), which reveals God as the ultimate Manager. This intellectual realization fosters profound gratitude (*shukr*) by observing how blessings are diverted to others, thereby confirming God's selective favor, and culminates in the longing for the *Liqa'* (meeting) with God, grounded in the assurance that the Bestower of such distinct honor will not forget His servant.
